extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners and patent applicants/draft attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and examining patent claims under the Korean Patent Act, focusing on support by the description, clarity and conciseness, special claim types (Markush, functional, parameter, composition/alloy), and formal claim dependency rules. Primarily for examiners but also instructive for applicants/drafters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of invention based on claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of the invention for which patent protection is sought shall be made based on the limitations recited in each of the claims in accordance with the applicant’s will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description or drawings are considered only when the claims are indefinite or technical terms are ambiguous. The invention should not be determined based on disclosure in the description beyond the limitations of the claims. An abstract cannot be used to decide the protection scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description (Article 42(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall be supported by the description of the invention; an invention recited in claims but not disclosed in the description would be unfair to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner shall determine whether a person skilled in the art can figure out the subject matters corresponding to the claims from the description. Support is assessed by whether the claimed invention departs from the scope grasped by a skilled person based on the description, not by literal identicalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: claim limitations neither disclosed nor implied
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the subject matters or the limitations of the claims are neither disclosed nor implied in the description of the invention, the claims are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: specific numerical limitations in claims absent in description; claims directed to an ultrasonic motor when description only discloses a DC motor (unless description implies other motors and a skilled person could practice with an ultrasonic motor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: differing terms causing ambiguous correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the terms used in the claims are different from those used in the description so that correspondence between description and claims is ambiguous, the claims are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity in terminology undermines the support requirement; examiner should assess whether a skilled person can bridge the terminology gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: claims recite functions/means without disclosed configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims recite means or steps to perform particular functions, but specific configuration corresponding to such means or steps is not disclosed in the description, the claims are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional recitation without any enabling structural or procedural disclosure can render claims unsupported unless the description enables the skilled person to realize the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: disclosure cannot be extended/generalized to claimed scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Where disclosure of the description cannot be extended or generalized to the scope of the claimed invention based on the level of skill in the art at filing, the claims are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: claims defined by technical effects (e.g., energy efficiency) but description only discloses specific means and cannot be generalized; claims reciting many chemical compounds defined by a property when only a few have demonstrated efficacy (collagenase-3 inhibitor example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported: omission of indispensable features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims do not recite the features explained as indispensable to solve the technical problem in the description, the claims are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: description requires a low-water-content 'cream' as stuffing to prevent moisture transition, but claims recite merely 'cream' (general milk fat substance), omitting the indispensable low-water-content feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to lack of description provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to interplay between Article 42(4)(i) (support) and Article 42(3)(i) (lack of description on claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the section discussing the relation with lack of description on claims for cross-reference when assessing support vs lack of description issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and concise statement requirement (Article 42(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must set forth the claimed invention clearly and concisely so they serve the function of determining protection scope and permit assessment of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether claims are clear and concise is determined by a person skilled in the art based on the claims in light of the description, drawings, and the level of skill at filing. 'Concise' refers to claim language, not to the idea of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear claim language but clerical error exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If unclear claim language is a mere clerical error and does not lead a skilled person to decide the invention is unclear, and the invention can be easily understood from description/drawings/skill level, it shall not be deemed unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of clerical errors and handling are provided; examiner should not issue a rejection for clerical errors and may make an ex officio amendment if no other ground exists. If uncertain, notify applicant to allow amendment/argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear: listing of claim elements without relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Where each claim element is merely listed but relationships between elements are not recited and therefore the invention is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must express relationships among elements (e.g., order, connection, interaction) rather than only listing constituent parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear: ambiguous category of claimed invention (product vs method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the category to which the claimed invention belongs is unclear, the claim is unclear. Category is usually determined by terms at the end of the claim, but may be ambiguous where subject matter hampers identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For products, a variety of expressions can be used to explain structure/function; for methods, various expressions explain method/steps. Determine category from claim wording; if difficult, deem ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear: excessive claim length or repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claim language is too lengthy, such as repetition of the same matter, so that the subject matter for which protection is sought is not clear and concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary repetition and overly long claim phrasing which obscures what is being claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear: expressions that make configuration unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims include expressions which make the configuration of the invention unclear, the claim may be indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the unclear expressions' meaning is clearly supported by the description and the invention is deemed clearly defined, the claim is acceptable. Examples of such expressions and how to assess them are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problematic vague qualifiers and optional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of arbitrarily additional matter or optional phrases (e.g., 'at one’s will', 'if necessary', 'in particular', 'for example', 'and/or') can render claims unclear or lead to multiple alternative inventions in a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether usage of 'and/or' or similar phrases results in multiple contrasting inventions in one claim and whether the number of claims is proper for the invention's characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problematic comparative/degree expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of vague comparative or degree expressions (e.g., 'mainly', 'as main process', 'appropriate', 'proper amount of', 'many', 'high', 'most of', 'almost', 'approximately', 'about') can render the claim unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such terms should be used carefully and clarified by the specification where necessary to avoid indefiniteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problematic negative limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of unclear negative limitations (e.g., 'except for', 'other than') can make the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure negative limitations are precise and supported by the disclosure to avoid ambiguity about what is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problematic numerical limitations without bounds or contradictory ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical limitations stated without maximum/minimum bounds (e.g., 'more than', 'less than', '0~10') or dual/conflicting numerical ranges in a single claim can render claims unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include '120-200℃ or more appropriately 150-180℃' — dual ranges in one claim create ambiguity. Provide precise numerical bounds or clarify intent in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear subject of indication (pronoun/reference ambiguity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the subject of indication is unclear (e.g., use of 'said gear' when multiple gear types were recited), the configuration of the invention is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify antecedents clearly; avoid ambiguous referencing pronouns or 'said' without clear antecedent. If clerical and understandable by skilled person, may be remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear due to reuse of same term for different functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple technical terms of the same expression serving different functions are used in the claims without specifying different functions or indicating corresponding reference numerals, the invention is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate identical expressions used for distinct roles or attach reference numerals to clarify meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear due to recitation of irrelevant non-technical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Where matters irrelevant to the technical configuration (commercial benefits, regions of sale, places of sale, etc.) are recited in claims, the invention is not clear and concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be limited to technical features relevant to the invention; exclude commercial/market statements from claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear when claim defined solely by reference to spec/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention is defined by reference to the description or drawings without reciting the configuration, the claim is unclear and may be invalid unless such reference is inevitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to description/drawings is allowable only if inevitable; otherwise the claim must recite the technical configuration explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical error categories (exceptions to rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain clerical errors are not deemed to violate clarity/conciseness and should not be a ground for rejection: (i) 'said OOO' lacking antecedent but invention clear when read excluding 'said'; (ii) non-identical but corresponding indicated/indicating terms; (iii) deleted dependent claims but invention still clear when excluding dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such clerical errors are found, examiner should not issue decision to reject and may make ex officio amendment if no other ground exists; if uncertain, notify applicant to allow response. If clerical errors arise from amendments, they should not be a new ground for rejection under Article 51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling uncertain clerical cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is unclear that a claim falls under the clerical-error exceptions, the examiner should notify the applicant of such facts and issue notice of ground for rejection rather than making an ex officio amendment or 'Matters to be noted', to give applicant opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after re-examination following applicant's response the claim is deemed to fall under clerical error exception, do not reject and consider ex officio amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claims acceptable when alternatives share property/function
rubrics_metrics.description: A Markush type claim selecting alternatives from a group does not render the claim indefinite if all inventions configured by selecting an alternative possess a similar property or function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A+(one of a, b, or c) is acceptable if A+a, A+b, A+c have similar properties/functions. The same principle applies beyond chemistry (e.g., mechanical, electrical fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical Markush grouping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical substances grouped in a Markush claim, the grouping does not render the claim indefinite if (①) all substances selected share a common property/vitality and (②) they share an important chemical structure or belong to a group deemed one in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Important chemical structure' means a common structural part prominent in most structures; 'group deemed as one' means substances expected by ordinary skill to be identically practiced in the claimed invention (i.e., same result expected whichever is chosen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional limitations — allowed only when configuration still clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims including functional limitations (reciting function or effect) are not allowable if the configuration is not clear; they are allowable when (①) defining functionally is necessary because the technical idea cannot be clearly set forth only by configuration (e.g., some biotech or computer-related inventions) or (②) the meaning of the functional limitation is clearly specified by the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall determine whether the subject matter is clearly understood by a skilled person in light of the description/drawings and the level of skill at filing; if not, issue rejection under Article 42(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product claims defined by manufacturing method
rubrics_metrics.description: A product claim can define the product by its manufacturing method if the product's configuration is clearly understood from the method limitation; otherwise the claim is indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If method-of-manufacture limitation does not make the product's structure/nature understandable even in light of the specification, drawings, and ordinary skill, examiner shall notify ground for rejection. If applicant must define product by process for specific reasons or proves process does not affect product structure/nature, examiner may consider rejection remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter inventions — special support/clarity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameter inventions include applicant-created parameters to indicate characteristics not generally used; such inventions are deemed not clear and concise except where (①) parameter's definition/technical meaning is clearly understood, (②) the inevitable reason for using the parameter is clearly shown, and (③) relationship with level of skill at filing is understood in light of description/drawings and skill level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show inevitability, include comparative examples satisfying and not satisfying the parameter and explain parameter-effect relationship and technical problem solved. To show relation to skill level, include comparative examples for known materials or logical explanation demonstrating exclusion. If understandable considering ordinary skill even without explicit disclosure, examiner may accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition ratio (%) — technical contradictions render claim unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims reciting composition ratios as percentages, certain technical deficiencies/contradictions render the claimed configuration not exactly stated: (①) sum of maximum ratios <100%; (②) sum of minimum ratios >100%; (③) sum of maximum of one component and minimums of others >100%; (④) sum of minimum of one component and maximums of others <100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open ('comprising') claims may be clear in some of these cases because unspecified other components can make totals 100%. Examples illustrate when percentage-based claims are indefinite vs acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts by weight and composition ratio clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing composition ratio as parts by weight does not require satisfying percentage-sum rules; parts by weight indicate amounts relative to a reference component and are deemed clear even without specifying the reference component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alloy claims are an exception: an alloy claim should set composition ranges that add up to 100% and cannot be specified only by limiting main component; total sum of composition ranges should not be over or under 100% regardless of 'comprising' or 'consisting of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy claim special rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For alloy claims, the composition ranges of each component should add up to 100%; even open claims ('comprising') are not accepted if the sum of ranges cannot reach 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, when claiming alloys, list components and recite composition ranges exactly. See the guidance for invention relating to alloy for further requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting: independent vs dependent claim discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim should narrow or add further limitations to specify the independent claim. If a claim does not narrow/add limitations in content, or formally refers to another claim without narrowing, it is not a dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a claim substituting element A with B in invention of claim 0 does not narrow/specify and thus is not a dependent claim. Article 5(1) of the Enforcement Decree prescribes that dependent claims must substantiate the independent claim by narrowing or adding limitations.
